mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) rise above 6.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which pressure corporate margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below zero signals supply-side weakness, which reduces earnings growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous demand expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month moving average of the federal funds rate rising above 5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, which increases discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous earnings expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) decline exceeding 1% signals labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 10% signals weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous supply expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month moving average of the federal funds rate rising above 5% combined with a year-over-year CPI increase above 3% signals a tightening monetary cycle with inflationary pressure, which increases discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous earnings expansion.
